preconditions.description: n is the count of forbidden prefix products, m is the modulus, and they satisfy 0 ≤ n < m ≤ 200,000

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= x < m for x in forbidden) if n > 0 else True
preconditions.description: if n > 0, the forbidden list contains n distinct integers between 0 and m - 1; otherwise, the forbidden list is empty

preconditions.expression: forbidden == sorted(set(forbidden)) if n > 0 else True
preconditions.description: the forbidden list contains distinct integers (no duplicates)

postconditions.description: output consists of exactly two lines: the first line is the sequence length k, the second line is the sequence itself

postconditions.expression: k == int(stdout_lines[0]) and all(0 <= int(x) < m for x in stdout_lines[1].split())
postconditions.description: the first line is an integer k (length of sequence), and the second line contains k space-separated integers between 0 and m - 1

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= (product := 1) < m for _ in range(k) for product in [product * int(x) % m])
postconditions.description: all prefix products modulo m are valid integers in [0, m - 1]

postconditions.expression: len({(product := 1) for _ in range(k) for product in [product * int(x) % m]}) == k
postconditions.description: all prefix products modulo m are distinct

postconditions.expression: all((product := 1) not in forbidden for _ in range(k) for product in [product * int(x) % m])
postconditions.description: no prefix product modulo m appears in the forbidden list
the sequence length k is maximized, where max_possible_length(stdin) is the largest possible k satisfying Q3, Q4, and Q5 for the given input
